docRequirement: goal.md:129 binds the post-turn evaluator's yes to a terminal outcome: "**Yes**: Claude Code clears the goal and records an achieved entry in the transcript." Reinforced at :13 ("The goal clears automatically once the condition is met") and in the comparison table at :28 (`/goal` — "Stops when: A model confirms the condition is met"). The page also binds a user entry point — `/goal <condition>` sets it (:42-52), `/goal clear` removes it (:98), bare `/goal` shows condition, elapsed, turns evaluated, token spend and the evaluator's most recent reason (:78-94) — and states that completion is "decided by a fresh model rather than the one doing the work" (:34).
current:
The mechanism exists as a Pi-harness session goal service with a post-settlement evaluator and an auto-continuation loop, but the evaluator has no terminal authority and there is no user surface.

1. On a yes, the goal stays active. `GoalService.evaluateAtSettlement` commits at packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/goal-service.ts:248-259 by spreading `...current`, so `status` remains `'active'`; it only writes `lastEvaluation: evaluation('evaluator', parsed.complete ? 'complete_suggested' : 'not_complete', ...)` (:252-258).
2. Only a manual command can terminate. `terminalGoal` (goal-service.ts:343-359) has exactly two callers, both in the same file: `action === 'complete'` (:151-155) and `action === 'cancel'` (:157-159). `terminalGoal` hardcodes `evaluation('manual', ...)` at :357.
3. The persistence validator structurally forbids an evaluator-sourced completion: `validTerminalState` (goal-service.ts:551-561) requires, for `status === 'complete'`, `evaluation.source === 'manual' && evaluation.verdict === 'completed' && evaluation.evidence.length > 0` (:555).
4. The evaluator is told it is advisory: `evaluatorPrompt` emits "Advisory goal check only. You have no tools and cannot change goal state." (goal-service.ts:480).
5. The consequence is a real extra turn. `SessionManager.schedulePiGoalContinuation` (packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:3360-3411) awaits `evaluateAtSettlement` at :3376 (evaluator model = `managed.agent.runMiniCompletion`, :3379), re-reads `service.safeSnapshot()` at :3383 and gates only on `status !== 'active'`; `canContinue` (goal-service.ts:264-271) checks settled + active + id/revision match and never inspects the verdict, so the fresh post-evaluation revision matches and :3398 dispatches another full turn via `sendMessage`. The only nudge is textual: `continuationPrompt` (goal-service.ts:273-282) appends `Last evaluation: complete_suggested: <reason>` and "Use Goal complete only with concrete evidence".
6. `complete_suggested` has zero consumers. `grep -ran complete_suggested apps packages` finds it only at the producer (goal-service.ts:254), three type/parser allowlists (packages/core/src/types/pi-harness-runtime.ts:114, packages/shared/src/protocol/pi-harness-runtime.ts:139, packages/shared/src/sessions/types.ts:106, goal-service.ts:608) and one test that LOCKS the behaviour (packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/goal-service.test.ts:146, in the case named "runs the advisory evaluator only when settled and never grants terminal authority", :128-146).
7. No user surface exists. `grep -ran goal_create apps packages` finds the action only in the wire type (packages/core/src/types/pi-harness-runtime.ts:346), its parser (packages/shared/src/protocol/pi-harness-runtime.ts:295) and the SessionManager control arm (SessionManager.ts:3279-3285, which does stamp `source: 'user', creator: 'desktop'`); no renderer sends it. The only shipped producer is the pi-only `Goal` tool (packages/session-tools-core/src/tool-defs.ts:991, description :644) whose port hardcodes `source: 'agent', creator: 'pi'` (SessionManager.ts:12148-12156). `PiHarnessRuntimeSnapshotV1.goal` (core/src/types/pi-harness-runtime.ts:308) and the `'goal'` invalidation domain (:12) exist but nothing in apps/electron/src/renderer or packages/ui reads them — the only renderer files matching "goal" are unrelated turn-card prose (packages/ui/src/components/chat/TurnCard.tsx:310).
8. Ours bounds the loop where Claude's does not: `DEFAULT_PI_GOAL_BUDGETS` (goal-service.ts:14-19) caps a goal at 32 turns / 250k tokens / $20 / 2h and `enforceBudgetsLocked` (:284-294) terminates it as `budget_exhausted`.
divergence:
Not a key-name or value mismatch — a missing state transition plus a validator that forbids it.

(a) On `parsed.complete === true` we write verdict `complete_suggested` and keep `status: 'active'` (goal-service.ts:248-259) where the page requires clearing the goal and recording an achieved entry. The correct enum value already exists in every schema (`completed` / `status: 'complete'`), so no wire type changes; only which value the evaluator branch produces.
(b) Even if (a) were flipped, `validTerminalState` (:555) would reject the record on reload because it demands `evaluation.source === 'manual'`. So the fix is two edits in one file, not one line.
(c) The evidence invariant the page implies is already satisfied on the evaluator path: `parseEvaluatorResult` calls `evidenceList(record.evidence, record.complete)` (:498), so `complete: true` with empty evidence is already downgraded to `not_complete` (locked by goal-service.test.ts:154-155). Nothing new is needed there.
(d) The "records an achieved entry in the transcript" half is entirely absent — no transcript/receipt entry and no `['goal']` domain invalidation is emitted when a goal terminates.
(e) Wider than filed: the page's whole premise (the USER types a condition, a FRESH model decides completion) has no surface here. There is no `/goal`, no `/goal clear`, no status view; only the model can create a goal, and only the model can complete it — the loop is model-owned end to end.
(f) Narrower than filed in one respect, and this is a deliberate superset, not a defect: our extra spend is capped by budgets (goal-service.ts:14-19, :284) where Claude's `/goal` is uncapped. Keep it.
(g) Cosmetic only: `MAX_CONDITION` is 8_192 (goal-service.ts:21) against the documented 4,000-character limit (:72) — more permissive, no user-visible divergence.

change.what: Give the evaluator terminal authority on a yes. Add an `evaluationSource: PiGoalEvaluationV1['source']` parameter to `terminalGoal` (it hardcodes `evaluation('manual', ...)` at :357) and pass `'manual'` from the two existing call sites (:153, :157). In `evaluateAtSettlement`'s final `exclusive` block, branch: when `parsed.complete` is true commit `terminalGoal(current, 'complete', 'completed', parsed.reason, parsed.evidence, now, 'evaluator')` instead of the active-status spread at :248-259; keep the existing `not_complete` spread unchanged for false. `terminalGoal` already applies `withElapsed`, so accounting closes correctly. Keep `complete_suggested` in the verdict union at :608 so already-persisted state still parses.

Line :555 must accept an evaluator-sourced completion: `if (goal.status === 'complete') return (evaluation.source === 'manual' || evaluation.source === 'evaluator') && evaluation.verdict === 'completed' && evaluation.evidence.length > 0;`. Leave `cancelled`, `blocked` and `budget_exhausted` requiring their current sources. Without this edit the new record is dropped on reload.

Line :480 now states something false. Replace "Advisory goal check only. You have no tools and cannot change goal state." with wording that keeps the no-tools constraint and drops the no-authority claim, e.g. "Goal completion check. You have no tools; judge only from the evidence below." The substring `You have no tools` is asserted by goal-service.test.ts:141 — keep it. Two things. (1) No new stop logic is needed — the `goal.status !== 'active'` guard at :3384 and `canContinue` at :3385 already abort the dispatch once the service terminates the goal; prove it with a test rather than adding a second guard. (2) Add the missing achieved entry. The `'goal'` domain invalidation ALREADY fires on every commit from the persist callback (`getOrCreatePiGoalService`, :2781), so do not add another; what is missing is the transcript record. After :3380, when the returned state's `goal.status === 'complete'` and `lastEvaluation.source === 'evaluator'`, append an achieved entry through the existing `appendPiExecutionReceipt` path (:2963, used at :12010) and return before dispatching a continuation. blastRadius:
Crosses a PERSISTENCE boundary — a risk trigger in this repo. `goalState` is a persisted session key (packages/shared/src/sessions/types.ts:48 key list, :387 field) hydrated through `parseGoalStateV1` (goal-service.ts:514-549) and `GoalService`'s constructor (:60-72), wired by `SessionManager.getOrCreatePiGoalService` (SessionManager.ts:2768-2784, persist callback :2776-2777). Downgrade hazard: a goal completed by the new code carries `status: 'complete'` + `lastEvaluation.source: 'evaluator'`, which TODAY'S `validTerminalState` (:555) rejects — `parseGoalStateV1` then returns undefined and the ENTIRE goal record is silently dropped on load by an older build. It does NOT cross the wire schema: `completed` is already a legal verdict in all three unions (core/src/types/pi-harness-runtime.ts:114, shared/src/protocol/pi-harness-runtime.ts:139, shared/src/sessions/types.ts:106).

Tests that will need re-reading: packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/goal-service.test.ts, packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.pi-runtime-snapshot.test.ts:167-192 (asserts `status: 'complete'` via the manual `goal_complete` path — unaffected but adjacent), packages/shared/src/protocol/pi-harness-runtime.test.ts:55-68, packages/server-core/src/sessions/rewind.test.ts:43/184. userImpact: Pi sessions only, and only after the model has set a goal with the pi-only `Goal` tool — there is no way for a user to set one. When it happens: the evaluator says the condition is met and the session KEEPS WORKING. SessionManager dispatches another full billed turn shown as "Continue active goal (<id>@<rev>)" (SessionManager.ts:3388, :3398), carrying `Last evaluation: complete_suggested: <reason>` in the prompt, and keeps dispatching after every settlement until the model itself calls `Goal complete` or a budget trips. So a goal whose work is demonstrably finished can burn turns up to 32 turns / 250k tokens / $20 / 2h and then end as `budget_exhausted` rather than complete — a successful goal recorded as a budget failure. The user has no way to see or stop this short of stopping the session: no `/goal` command, no status view, no achieved entry in the transcript, and no UI reads `PiHarnessRuntimeSnapshotV1.goal`. What they experience is an agent that will not stop and a chat that keeps producing turns with no visible reason. Whether it surfaces at all depends on the model volunteering `Goal complete` promptly — in the common case it costs one extra turn, in the bad case it costs the whole budget.
